card werk-base-dir  [decided]
v0 grows in its own directory beside the prototype, with its own packages and checks
why: v0 needs a clean project with nothing from the prototype, and the build runs inside the prototype's repository.

v0 has its own package list, lockfile, compiler and test configuration in one top-level directory. Nothing in it imports from the prototype. Every check runs inside that directory and installs its packages first when they are missing. Moving v0 to its own repository is a copy of that one directory. See #werk-base for why v0 is a new project.

card werk-base-repo  [decided]
v0 is built in a new git repository whose main branch starts with zero files
why: A repository of its own shares no files, history or map state with the prototype, so nothing of the prototype can become v0's base.

The main line of every #werk build is the main branch of a new git repository, separate from the prototype's repository (#st-plan-main). Its first commit holds no files. The spec and the first tickets set up the project from that empty tree: the package files, the build and test targets, and the folder layout.

The prototype stays in its own repository. A builder may read it as a reference (#werk-base), but no build starts from it and nothing merges into it.

  -> refines         werk-base  v0 is a new project, built from scratch in its own repository
  -> depends_on      st-plan-main  Tickets merge straight onto the main line, with no integration branch
       why: It names the repository whose main branch is the main line that #st-plan-main builds from and merges onto.
  <- alternative_to  werk-base-repo:opt0  Build v0 on the main branch of the prototype's repository, with the prototype on a sibling branch
  <- alternative_to  werk-base-repo:opt1  Build v0 on the main branch of this repository, with the prototype on a sibling branch that is deleted once v0 matches the map
Options
  werk-base-repo:opt0  Build v0 on the main branch of the prototype's repository, with the prototype on a sibling branch
    why not: The prototype's history, its map state and its files share one repository with v0, so a build can still start from or merge into the wrong tree.
  werk-base-repo:opt1  Build v0 on the main branch of this repository, with the prototype on a sibling branch that is deleted once v0 matches the map
    why not: The two lines share one repository, its history and its map state, so a build can still start from or merge into the prototype's tree. Only a separate repository makes that impossible.
----------
card werk-base  [decided]
v0 is a new project, built from scratch in its own repository
why: The current code is a prototype, iterated on to find the right shape. v0 is the clean implementation of that shape.
subtree: 3 cards, 3 decided

v0 starts in a new, empty repository. Nothing is ported from the prototype code.

- The spec is the decided cards that #werk depends on, not the prototype code.
- The prototype code is a reference. A builder may read it to see how a decided behaviour looks. It does not copy it.
- The stack is #werk-stack: React + Vite for the client, inside the Bun server from #werk-hmr. Vite transforms the client, so v0 has a client build step.

Why not extend the prototype: it works well as a product, but its code is messy. A clean build tests whether the decided cards are enough to rebuild the behaviour.

The fix is staged on `#werk-base-dir`. Press ✓ on that card to accept it, and ✕ on `#werk-base-dir-root`.

**Yes, the contradiction exists now, in two decided cards.**

- `#werk-base-dir` puts v0 "in one top-level directory" inside the prototype's repository. Its why says "the build runs inside the prototype's repository". It plans the move to a separate repository for later.
- `#werk-base-repo` puts v0 in a new repository that starts empty. No build starts from the prototype, and nothing merges into it.

Both cannot hold: v0 is a directory in the prototype's repository, or it is a separate repository. The code chose the separate repository. `werk-v0` is its own repository, with `package.json`, `bun.lock` and `tsconfig.json` at its root.

How it happened: `#werk-base-dir` was proposed first, on 2026-10-19 at 00:16. `#werk-base-repo` was proposed and accepted at 13:00 that day. `#werk-base-dir` was accepted two days later, on 2026-10-21. Nothing noticed that its location was already out of date. No link joins the two cards, so the second card put no mark on the first.

**What is still true in `#werk-base-dir`:** the isolation rule. v0 has its own packages, nothing imports from the prototype, and every check installs the locked packages first. The proposal keeps that rule. It changes only the location to "the root of v0's own repository" and removes the plan to move v0 later.

**Two items wait until you accept:**

1. Link `#werk-base-dir` to `#werk-base-repo` with `depends_on`. The card now needs that repository. Without the edge, the next change to `#werk-base-repo` again marks nothing. I hold it because an edge on a decided card takes effect at once, before you accept.
2. `#werk-base-dir:opt0`, "Delete the prototype code from the build branch", assumes a shared repository. Its why_not no longer applies: no merge can reach the prototype. Removing it is your call.

Next: press ✓ on `#werk-base-dir`. Then I add the edge and we go to `#werk-fake-launch-role`.
